summary: Discovery focused on HarborBank's need for dedicated GPU capacity for customer-facing LLM features. Key topics: isolation/data residency, burst capacity for monthly batch jobs, autoscaling expectations, latency SLOs, security controls (SOC2/KMS/SAML), and pilot scope. Customer leans toward Dedicated with potential Private (VPC) for regulated workloads; next step is benchmark plan and pricing/commit discussion.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-04-09 16:00 PDT | Duration: ~45m | Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Miguel Santos (Redwood SE), Sarah Liu (HarborBank Head of ML), Devon Carter (Infra Lead), Priya Menon (CTO)

[00:00] Lena Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Lena from Redwood, AE on the account, and with me is Miguel our SE. How's everyone doing?
[00:07] Sarah Liu: Doing well, thanks. Excited to dig in, we, uh, we pushed this up after the execs saw your benchmarks.
[00:12] Miguel Santos: Great, thanks for the time. High level today we want to understand your workload shape, isolation requirements, burst/baseline needs and any compliance constraints so we can recommend Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private.
[00:22] Priya Menon: From a top level, we have two sets of workloads: real-time customer chat for banking support and nightly large batch enrichments for analytics. The chat needs low latency, the batch needs GPUs for cost-effective token throughput.
[00:35] Devon Carter: Yep, and we have strict controls on customer PII — requirement for audit logs and KMS for keys. We also prefer dedicated tenancy for some regulated products.
[00:45] Miguel Santos: Makes sense. Quick qual Qs: current model infra? are you running anything self-hosted or using APIs now?
[00:52] Sarah Liu: We're hybrid. A lot of R&D on internal infra on GCP and some experiments with hosted APIs (we tested OpenAI for prototyping). Production readiness is the blocker — cost and, frankly, data controls.
[01:08] Lena Park: Got it. When you say dedicated tenancy: are you looking for Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pools we operate) or full Private (VPC or on-prem) where you control the networking?
[01:19] Priya Menon: Initially Dedicated is preferred if we get isolation and contractual controls. Private could be for the higher-risk products later.
[01:27] Miguel Santos: For Dedicated we offer reserved GPU pools with tenant isolation and optional VPC peering. You can pin model versions, and we support KMS-backed encryption for models and logs. There's also a burst option — customers reserve baseline capacity and enable burst to shared capacity in peak times, or use dedicated burst nodes with warm pools.
[01:42] Devon Carter: How does that burst behave? We run heavy end-of-month processing for compliance reporting — spikes can be 5x baseline for short windows. We can't tolerate extreme throttling.
[01:52] Miguel Santos: Good question. We typically architect with a baseline committed capacity sized for the 95th percentile steady traffic, and then a burst buffer for short spikes. For example, customers often reserve 4 GPUs baseline and configure 2-4 GPUs as burst. For predictable monthly spikes we can provision scheduled burst nodes to avoid cold starts. There are tradeoffs on cost — dedicated burst nodes are more predictable but pricier.
[02:12] Sarah Liu: Do you support autoscaling when latency SLO is tight? Chat needs 90th percentile <200ms for short prompts.
[02:18] Miguel Santos: Yes — our runtime supports latency-aware autoscaling with continuous batching. For ultra-low p99 you typically pin a smaller model variant or use more GPUs per replica to keep per-token latency low. Also KV cache and prefix caching reduce repeated token costs and latency for short-turn chat.
[02:34] Priya Menon: We have a strict SLO for login-time chat flows. Can you guarantee failover to a hosted fallback if our Dedicated pool is saturated?
[02:44] Lena Park: Absolutely. We support routing policy to fall back to a hosted model variant or a lower-cost region. That can be configured per route with automatic triggers. We can also set alerts to notify infra when fallbacks happen.
[02:57] Devon Carter: On security, we need SOC2 compliance and want to review audit log granularity. Do you capture token-level logs or only request metadata?
[03:06] Miguel Santos: By default we capture request metadata and sanitized logs. For Dedicated we can enable token-level logging with customer-controlled retention, and KMS integration for encryption at rest. We also integrate with customer's SIEM via secure log forwarding.
[03:19] Sarah Liu: Any certifications for the Private path? For some products we'll require the control plane inside our VPC or on-prem.
[03:25] Lena Park: Private gives you a customer-managed control plane option and on-prem deployments are available for air-gapped/regulatory scenarios. Those come with an enterprise license and a support model.
[03:34] Miguel Santos: Back to sizing: can you share a rough QPS for chat and token/sec for batch?
[03:40] Sarah Liu: Chat is about 40 rps at peak, avg 12 rps. Prompts are usually short, 40-80 tokens. Batch runs consume ~20M tokens over a 2-hour window monthly — so peak token throughput is high but predictable.
[03:53] Miguel Santos: Ok that pattern maps well to reserved baseline for chat and scheduled burst for batch windows. Example config: 6x A100-style GPUs baseline gives you consistent latency for chat; scheduled 8-12 GPU burst for the 2-hour batch. We would run a benchmark to confirm model variant and quantization options.
[04:11] Devon Carter: What about model variants and quantization? We need to keep output quality high for customer-facing flows.
[04:17] Miguel Santos: We recommend a mixed strategy: higher-precision or larger model for chat SLO, quantized variants for batch to save cost, and reranking/light-weight models for filtering. Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization profiles based on the sample prompts you share.
[04:30] Priya Menon: Licensing and contracts — what are the commitment tiers for Dedicated? Annual? Monthly?
[04:36] Lena Park: We offer monthly and annual reserved capacity tiers. Annual has better unit pricing and commit discounts. We can also do a short pilot (30-60 days) with a smaller reserved commit and then scale to full dedication.
[04:47] Sarah Liu: For pilot we want a POC where you run our top prompts and our traffic pattern, and we measure latency, cost per token, and failure modes.
[04:55] Miguel Santos: That's straightforward. For the POC we'll need sample prompts, an example traffic trace, and credentials to run a synthetic load against a dedicated test pool. We'll share a benchmark plan that includes p50/p90/p99 latency and token throughput.
[05:08] Devon Carter: Network-wise we'll want VPC peering and private IP connectivity. Is that supported for Dedicated?
[05:14] Miguel Santos: Yes, Dedicated supports VPC peering and private endpoints. For Private deployments we support deploy-in-customer-VPC and on-prem if needed.
[05:21] Sarah Liu: How about data residency? Some of our EU customers must remain in EU. Can you pin region?
[05:26] Lena Park: Yes, region pinning is supported at deployment level. With Dedicated we can provision pools in specific regions and enforce routing policies to keep traffic inside region.
[05:35] Priya Menon: Cost question — how does pricing handle burst nodes? If we enable scheduled burst, is that billed differently?
[05:41] Lena Park: Scheduled burst nodes are billed at dedicated rates when provisioned. There's also a pay-as-you-go burst option that uses shared capacity at a different unit cost. We'll send a pricing sheet showing baseline commit vs dedicated burst vs shared burst pricing.
[05:55] Sarah Liu: In terms of operational visibility, what kind of dashboards and traces do we get?
[06:00] Miguel Santos: Redwood Console gives per-route/model dashboards, token-level cost breakdowns, per-request traces and KV cache hit rates. You can hook into tracing and error analysis. We also provide rollout controls for canaries and automatic fallback policies.
[06:13] Devon Carter: Are there known gotchas with warm start for large quantized models? We want predictable cold-start times.
[06:20] Miguel Santos: Cold starts for very large models can be long; we mitigate with warm pools and continuous batching. For scheduled batch runs we recommend pre-warming nodes. Also model compilation and kernel selection step is done ahead of time during onboarding to reduce surprises.
[06:35] Priya Menon: From a timeline standpoint: we're targeting a pilot in May and production by July if POC looks good. Is that realistic?
[06:42] Lena Park: That's realistic. Pilot in May — we'll scope the POC this month, run benchmarks early May, then iterate on sizing and SLAs with you.
[06:50] Sarah Liu: Ok good. One more: how do you handle sensitive PII in prompts? We need to ensure no retention and deletion hooks.
[06:58] Miguel Santos: We support prompt redaction, on-demand data deletion, and configurable retention windows. For Dedicated we can configure no persistent logging and only forward minimal metadata if requested.
[07:10] Devon Carter: Integration: we use HashiCorp Vault for secrets and AWS KMS for some keys. Supports?
[07:16] Miguel Santos: Yes, we have KMS integrations and support Vault for secret rotation; we can walk through the integration pattern in the security review.
[07:24] Priya Menon: Are there SLAs for latency or availability?
[07:28] Lena Park: Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and latency targets based on commit tier. We'll include SLA language in the pricing packet.
[07:36] Sarah Liu: Competitors: We evaluated Anthropic and Bedrock briefly. Anthropic had limitations on deployment flexibility and Bedrock's cost model wasn't predictable for heavy token workloads.
[07:48] Miguel Santos: Noted. We'll highlight how Dedicated helps with predictable unit economics and consistent latency.
[07:55] Lena Park: Next steps recap: we'll send Dedicated pricing + T&C, Miguel will send benchmark plan and required artifacts, and you (Sarah) will provide prompt set and traffic trace. We'll schedule POC scoping call for the week of April 20th.
[08:09] Sarah Liu: Sounds good. We'll try to get the prompt set by Tuesday.
[08:12] Devon Carter: One last quick thing — do you support model version pinning and rollback?
[08:16] Miguel Santos: Yes, you can pin model versions and do canary rollouts; automated rollback on quality regressions is supported if you provide eval hooks.
[08:26] Priya Menon: Ok thanks everyone, this was useful.
[08:30] Lena Park: Thanks all — we'll follow up with the deck, pricing, and benchmark plan.
[08:35] (call ends)

Notes on transcript quality: medium — some overlapping speech and a few transcriber errors (names, acronyms).
